title: 7-Day Perfectionism Reset
description: When everything has to be perfect, nothing gets done. This program dismantles the perfectionism trap one day at a time.
outcomes: Recognize perfectionism as fear, not standards

days.title: The Terrible First Draft
days.insight: Perfectionism isn't high standards — it's fear disguised as virtue. You're not trying to be excellent; you're trying to avoid the vulnerability of being seen trying.
days.action: Do ONE thing badly on purpose today. Send that email without re-reading it twice. Write that messy paragraph. Notice: the world didn't end.
days.reflectionQuestion: What did you protect yourself from by not doing this before?

days.title: The 70% Standard
days.insight: The 70% rule: if it's 70% good enough, ship it. The last 30% takes 80% of the time and rarely changes outcomes.
days.action: Pick one task you've been overthinking. Do it to 70% and STOP. Walk away. Notice the discomfort — that's your perfectionism, not your standards.
days.reflectionQuestion: Where in your life are you spending 80% of effort on the last 30%?

days.title: Shipping the Thing
days.insight: Done is better than perfect. The world rewards completion, not excellence at the start.
days.action: Choose one thing that's been sitting in 'drafts' or 'in progress'. Publish it. Send it. Ship it. No revisions allowed.
days.reflectionQuestion: What would happen if this wasn't your last chance to get it right?

days.title: The Permission slip
days.insight: Perfectionists need permission to be imperfect. We're giving you that permission.
days.action: Write yourself a permission slip: 'I am allowed to do this badly. I am allowed to ship it. I am enough.'
days.reflectionQuestion: What have you been denying yourself permission to do?

days.title: Imperfect Action
days.insight: Action creates momentum. Perfection creates stagnation. Momentum beats perfection every time.
days.action: Do something related to your work in a way that's clearly imperfect. Record a video. Write a tweet. Make a粗糙 plan.
days.reflectionQuestion: What would you do today if you knew you couldn't fail?

days.title: Feedback Over Perfection
days.insight: Feedback is information. It's not judgment. It's how you improve. Perfectionism keeps you isolated. Feedback brings you connection.
days.action: Share something you've been working on with one person. Ask for one piece of feedback. No defensiveness allowed.
days.reflectionQuestion: What's the difference between feedback and criticism?

days.title: The Completion Ritual
days.insight: Completion is its own reward. It's the closing of a loop. Perfectionism keeps things open, unresolved.
days.action: Take one project that's 'almost done'. Mark it 'done'. Celebrate. Close the loop.
days.reflectionQuestion: What loop have you been keeping open that you need to close?
